Swiss Army Bench 0.0.22: a desktop app.

- **Swiss Army Bench is a desktop app now** (PySide6, its pages in Qt's built-in Chromium): a **Swiss Army Bench**
  entry with its icon in the Start menu (a launcher in ~/Applications on macOS, an app entry on Linux) opens it in
  app windows of its own, no browser tab. The Workbench and every pop-out are real windows; downloads ask where to
  save; Print to PDF, the clipboard and F12's developer tools work; an outside link opens in your browser.
  The browser is still there if you want it: **Open in browser** (Ctrl+Shift+B) or `swissarmybench open --browser`.
- **The server lives with the app:** it starts when you open Swiss Army Bench and stops when you close its last
  window. The agent, VS Code and `sab.push()` keep it up while they are working, and it stops 10 minutes after
  their last request with no window open. An open project's unsaved changes are saved first, as Autosave does.
- **The tray icon and start at sign-in are gone.** The first start removes what an older version left (the
  sign-in entry and the old tray icon) and says so once. Updates come through the app's own "Update available".
- **The rail is wider, with larger icons.**
- **Bigger install:** Qt's web engine adds about 650 MB (about 1.1 GB in all). `install.ps1 -Uninstall` (or
  `install.sh --uninstall`) removes the app and its Start menu entry.

Update from the page's "Update available" (Update to 0.0.22), or:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```
